audit_findings.title: The perimeter contract contradicts the partial-year Foot Locker economics
audit_findings.mechanism: The partial-year Foot Locker contribution enters anchor OE, while acquisition shares enter the denominator and the DCF represents the full post-acquisition business.
audit_findings.evidence: These results reflect the operations from the September 8, 2025 acquisition date through the end of fiscal 2025, which does not include the peak back-to-school selling season in August.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year mismatch is demonstrated: fiscal 2025 includes Foot Locker only from September 8, 2025 and excludes its August back-to-school season. The valuation discloses this and uses the lower actual anchor, but that conservatism does not establish the sustainable OE of the enlarged company. Full-year Foot Locker could add or subtract value because the acquired segment reported a $60.0 million partial-year net loss and a $14.4 million segment loss in the first half of fiscal 2026. The valuation effect is therefore unresolved but reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile full-year pro forma Foot Locker OE, maintenance investment and working-capital needs; rerun the valuation using the first complete post-acquisition fiscal year and supersede the partial-year valuation.

audit_findings.title: The $609.1 million stake add-back is not reconciled to identifiable investments
audit_findings.magnitude: $553.822 million unreconciled, computed as $609.1 million less the filed $50.0 million equity-method investment and $5.278 million available-for-sale security; approximately $6.00 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The $609.1 million is added directly through the equity bridge, dollar-for-dollar, rather than earned through OE.
audit_findings.evidence: These investments consist of $ 69.5 million of Foot Locker equity securities and $ 50.0 million for an equity method investment.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing reconciliation is demonstrated, although the exact composition and final error remain unresolved. The latest filing identifies a $50.0 million equity-method investment and a $5.278 million available-for-sale security. The former $111.6 million Foot Locker holding was retired in the acquisition, while deferred-compensation assets are matched by equal liabilities and pension assets support pension obligations. The unexplained $553.822 million equals about 5.0% of the $11.158 billion base equity value and exceeds the $0.44 per-share margin between bull value and market price, so it is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce a security-by-security bridge for all $609.1 million, remove the retired Foot Locker holding, and net restricted, pension, deferred-compensation or liability-matched assets; rerun all scenarios with only verified unencumbered non-operating investments.

audit_findings.title: Known post-anchor integration costs may have been stripped as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: $200 million expected fiscal-2026 acquisition-related charges, including $125.8 million incurred in the first half and $74.2 million remaining by subtraction
audit_findings.mechanism: If normalized out of anchor OE and omitted from forecast cash flows, the costs overstate near-term distributable OE without reducing the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect approximately $150 million of acquisition-related costs in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The future charges are filed, but their omission from the valuation is not demonstrated because the OE bridge was not supplied. The updated $200 million forecast equals 29.2% of the $685.8 million anchor, and $125.8 million had already been incurred in the first half. Even when treated as finite rather than recurring costs, omission is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion, particularly because bull value of $139.59 is only $0.44 above the market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $390.0 million historical and $125.8 million first-half charges through the OE bridge, identify cash versus noncash components, and rerun the DCF with any omitted remaining cash costs deducted in their expected periods.

audit_findings.title: A noncash Foot Locker investment gain could remain in the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.2 million filed gain; if retained and perpetuated, computed operating-value overstatement is approximately $449 million to $700 million, or $4.86 to $7.58 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: The noncash gain would inflate anchor OE and every forecast year generated from that anchor, while investment value may also be recognized through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded a non-cash gain of $ 42.2 million in fiscal 2025 related to these equity securities within other income on the Consolidated Statements of Income, resulting from net changes in Foot Locker’s underlying stock price during the respective periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The $42.2 million noncash gain is demonstrated, but whether it was removed from OE is unresolved. The method expressly purges interest income but does not document a separate removal of this gain. It equals 6.2% of anchor OE; capitalizing it through the supplied scenario multiples would materially overstate value and would reverse the bull scenario's narrow premium to market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $42.2 million from other income into the OE calculation and rerun all scenarios after removing it if it remains in the anchor, independently of the interest-income adjustment and stake bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquired claims ahead of common equity were still provisional
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the latest filed measurement-period adjustments reduced goodwill by $19.0 million but do not bound the remaining litigation exposure
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecognized or understated litigation and tax claims would reduce the equity bridge or future OE because they are cash claims senior to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The most significant areas of acquisition accounting not considered final are litigation contingencies, long-lived assets, and income taxes, which may impact the total goodwill recognized as well.
audit_findings.explanation: Provisional acquisition accounting is demonstrated, but no omitted cash liability is established. By August 1, 2026, long-lived assets and income taxes had been refined and litigation contingencies were the most significant unfinished area. The $19.0 million net goodwill adjustment had no significant income-statement effect, but it does not provide an upper bound on unresolved claims. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the final purchase-price allocation and reconcile all measurement-period litigation, tax, indemnity and assumed-liability updates to the latest balance sheet; deduct or forecast any incremental cash claim not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling combines share counts from mismatched dates
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 3.423937 million shares separate the 92.350493 million ceiling from the 88.926556 million August 28 cover count, a 3.85% spread; the exact overlap is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted exercised or vested awards inflate the per-share denominator and understate every scenario's value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: When options are exercised, the Company issues new shares of common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, and the first-half roll-forward shows 1.216 million option exercises and 0.379 million restricted shares vested after January 31. Those resulting shares may already be represented in the August cover count, while the ceiling adds the January award inventories again. The exact overlap cannot be calculated because withholding, repurchases, forfeitures and remaining awards require an August roll-forward. The possible 3.85% denominator spread is material relative to the bull scenario's 0.32% premium over market price.
audit_findings.action: Build an August 28 award roll-forward and add only options, restricted awards and performance awards still outstanding and not represented in the cover count; rerun per-share values with a date-consistent diluted denominator.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.2 million FY2017 residual, equal to 8.6% of FY2017 OE; current-anchor residual unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense depresses OE and therefore the operating-value calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $27.2m (11.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value, but the record does not classify the residual or quantify it for the current anchor. The only supplied amount, $27.2 million in FY2017, was 8.6% of that year's $315.1 million OE, which is not small enough to dismiss without evidence. Whether any residual qualifies for addition and whether the present effect is material remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Classify residual D&A by asset and year using filed depreciation disclosures; rerun OE and the valuation only for amounts demonstrated to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
